                    ### Question
                    Which of the following semi-solid pharmaceutical forms with which a master formula can be prepared has greater occlusivity ?:

                    ### Options
                    opa. Hydrophobic ointments
opb. Hydrophobic or water-oily creams.
opc. Hydrophilic or ole-aqueous creams.
opd. Hydrophilic ointments

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In evaluating the occlusivity of semi-solid pharmaceutical forms, hydrophobic ointments are known to have high lipid content, which forms a substantial barrier on the skin, effectively preventing water loss and providing greater occlusivity. This aligns with the consensus that lipid-rich formulations enhance skin barrier function. Hydrophobic or water-oily creams have moderate lipid content, offering some occlusivity but less than hydrophobic ointments. Hydrophilic or ole-aqueous creams, with low lipid content, provide minimal occlusivity due to their limited barrier formation. Hydrophilic ointments, being water-based, do not form a significant barrier and thus have low occlusivity. The retrieved evidence paths, while broad, support the role of lipids in barrier formation, reinforcing the consensus that lipid content is crucial for occlusivity. Therefore, hydrophobic ointments are the most occlusive option.
